aliases: perturbing a rule, not just a starting point
purpose: What survives when the correction rule itself changes?
meaning: Set each selected velocity rule equal to zero. Compare the number and local type of its equilibria with the zero-offset rule; the two explicit perturbation families illustrate different robustness.

definition.setting: Compare two toy alignment rules. One always pulls toward a shifted target; the other is balanced at a fold. Move a small offset in the rule rather than moving the starting position. One family keeps a single attracting balance point, while the critical family can gain or lose balance points.
conditions: This compares two explicit one-dimensional families on the line. The linear family retains one attracting equilibrium; the fold at ε=0 changes its equilibrium count under arbitrarily small signed shifts. This is a bounded introduction to structural stability, not a general certificate over all perturbations or domains.
The displayed calculation, coordinates and marks are evaluated from the same declared input state.
